text: Where access to credit is concerned, we had earlier extended measures like the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the Extended Support Scheme – Standardised to enable SMEs in affected sectors to defer principal payments on their eligible loans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I heard just now suggestions from Mr Don Wee and Mr Edward Chia to enhance some of these schemes and to extend the moratoriums for the loan schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, the MAS and our economic agencies assess that the credit market remains healthy and the current support measures are sufficient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will continue to monitor the situation closely and we will review the need for any adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, our local banks are proactively reaching out to SMEs to provide relief and restructuring support based on their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I also recognise that cash flow is a major concern for many SMEs and several Members highlighted this – I think Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Edward Chia and others.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will strive to push out the support as fast as we can.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do so within our operational limits, while ensuring accuracy and good governance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, Government's assistance is now flowing such that there is cash flow support to businesses throughout the year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we try to ensure a steady stream of cash payouts to businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There may be businesses or workers who do not meet the qualifying criteria of some of our schemes and that is why we have the COVID-19 Recovery Grant - Temporary to cater to individuals who may not fit into any of our schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, for example, hawkers in coffeeshops, they may not qualify for the Market and Hawker Relief Fund but they can apply for the COVID-19 Recovery Grant – Temporary and we will help them through that avenue.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also helping these hawkers through rental rebates, to support them through the online delivery platforms and many other ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, we also consider businesses which are badly affected but may not fall neatly into the specified SSIC codes, because these are the codes we use to determine which category the business is in and then we would disburse the JSS payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The codes may not accurately reflect the kinds of business activities that the firm is involved in.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, since the inception of JSS, we do consider appeals from businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of these groups, if they appealed, have been successful.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, if you know of such cases, you can let MOF know, you can appeal through IRAS and we will look at each case on its own merit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, agencies do exercise flexibility in implementation of the different schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With regard to the COVID-19 Recovery Grant – Temporary, for example, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Sharael Taha asked about more flexibility for those with extenuating circumstances, flexibility around the income loss or annual value criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Again, agencies will look at each case and consider it on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On rental relief, I recognise the difficult issues faced by landlords and tenants as Ms Jessica Tan had highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I had mentioned it in my Statement yesterday and perhaps it is worth repeating the principles for intervention.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The starting point is the sanctity of contract.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not lightly intervene and we do so only in specific situations and in a carefully scoped manner.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is also in line with Mr Cheng Hsing Yao's caution that we should not create the impression that such interventions are now becoming the norm.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, landlords and tenants have a symbiotic relationship where both parties do well or, conversely, do poorly together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is important to keep lines of communication open to ensure constructive discussions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we now have the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee that facilitates this by bringing together key representatives from Singapore's landlord and tenant communities to discuss issues related to retail lease agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, including Ms Janet Ang, Mr Edward Chia, Mr Don Wee, had suggestions on quite a wide range of measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will study these options for future support, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as many have also highlighted, the best way to help our businesses is to allow them to resume their operations and get their top line back again.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we do so and when we start to reopen our economy, reopen our borders, the manpower inflow will also resume.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will then address concerns about acute labour shortages in sectors like construction, marine shipyard and process, I think a point that Ms Janet Ang and Mr Melvin Yong highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, as these Members have noted, we have started several pilots to bring in migrant workers who would adhere to strict testing protocols in their home countries and then we bring them in safely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will explore expanding these pilots to facilitate worker inflow in a safe manner.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I do not have any concrete numbers with me but, obviously, the numbers are not going to be very large at this stage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will take time to do this in a safe and sustainable manner.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why, to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's question, it is not possible to do these development projects this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not because of financial issues, it is not because of money and then, we can borrow and, therefore, do some of these projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is just that the firms will not have workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we do not want to rush to bring in workers and then end up with a large outbreak again.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, no one can predict the trajectory of this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I have said just now, if we continue on our path of reopening, hopefully, we can continue it in a continuous manner but I cannot rule out the possibility of occasional slowdowns or even pull-backs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we do so, then we have to introduce additional restrictions and, at that stage, we will have to put in place another package to support businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we have to do that, then we will need to find ways to fund such a package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as Mr Liang Eng Hwa noted, it is becoming harder and harder to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You have to squeeze out the "next drop of funding".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Already, with this round, agencies have reviewed their development projects due to COVID-19-related delays; as I have said, it is not possible to do it this year because of manpower shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, those delays of projects have allowed us to reallocate resources for the current support measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, that is what we would do if we had to do another package within this financial year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Liang suggested setting up a pandemic economic response fund so we do not have to come to Parliament each time there is a support package and Mr Louis Chua, I think, also mentioned something similar with the idea of automatic stabilisers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It may be challenging to set up such a fund this year because we will not have the resources to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is an idea we can study for the next Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, we cannot rule out the possibility that the situation may significantly worsen.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides dealing with the immediate challenges, we must prepare for the next phase.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Life in a post-pandemic world will be different from what it used to be and we must expect greater uncertainty and volatility.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must continue this important work of transforming our economy and equipping our people with the skills they need in an age of change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we transition to this new normal, we must go beyond support measures, towards building strength and resilience for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must continue to invest in growing our economy, strengthening our society and greening our home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our first priority is to expand opportunities and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To do so, we need a strong and vibrant economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will enable us to provide a high quality of life for all Singaporeans and enable them to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a small and open economy, rapid shifts in the external environment have profound implications for Singapore and COVID-19 has brought this out acutely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Industries and firms have accelerated the restructuring of their supply chains to reduce concentration risks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remote working is becoming the new norm, reducing the importance of geographical factors in where companies choose to locate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this outcome will blunt our tax incentives to anchor significant activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of these trends can erode our value proposition as a hub economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recently attended the G20 Finance Ministers meeting in Venice.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Being in Venice, I was reminded of how a city's fortunes can easily change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Venice enjoyed great prosperity in the Middle Ages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was a vital trading hub, connecting the East with the West via the Mediterranean.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But Venice did not adapt fast enough to changes in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The invention of the seafaring galleon, which could survive at sea for months, even years, meant that European states could set up new oceanic trade routes, bypassing Venice altogether.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This marked the beginning of the decline of Venice.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What happened to Venice can happen to Singapore, too, if we are not careful.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must never take our hub status for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must continue to stay open and double down on our connectivity as a trusted hub for commerce, trade and talent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we thought that it was very important that we have the debate on the issue of free trade agreements (FTAs) not too long ago.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must continually work hard to strengthen our value proposition as the gateway to Asia and the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Across industries, too, rapid technological change is bringing about new waves of disruption.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As the global economy recovers, we are seeing increased levels of activity, start-up and company formation around the world, powered by new innovations and ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We see this happening in Singapore, too – I think a point that Mr Leon Perera highlighted just now.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will strive to anchor and nurture more of such activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been badly hit by the pandemic but, at some point, demand will return and the industry will recover.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, at that time, the future of the industry may be different.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we are seeing a shift towards sustainable aviation fuels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the longer term, we could even see the emergence of hydrogen-powered aircraft.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Digital services which leverage aircraft data to create new services, such as fuel optimisation and aircraft health monitoring, are also emerging.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We start from a position of strength with an established base of engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we cannot assume that this lead is going to be with us forever.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must actively pursue opportunities to anchor global Centres of Excellence with new technologies to ensure we remain a global node for aerospace MRO and manufacturing activities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we must help our local Singapore firms, our SMEs, to grow and build new capabilities to partner the multinational companies (MNCs) so that, together, we can have a vibrant aerospace ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This process of restructuring and transformation is vital to keeping our economy vibrant and strong.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the focus of our support measures will, over time, shift from providing pain relief, as we are now, to building deep capabilities for companies to innovate and transform.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To do this, we have a suite of capability development schemes administered by Enterprise Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recognise some Members have said that the schemes can be overwhelming and difficult to navigate; the process for administration can be cumbersome.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I want to assure Members that Enterprise Singapore takes all these feedback and suggestions seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have SME Centres, we have the Business Grant Portal and they will continue to look at the suggestions that Members have given to see how we can strengthen our SME sector and help even more of them scale up to new markets overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just as our firms are transforming, we must also envision jobs of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I think many Members of Parliament have spoken on this, including the Labour Members of Parliament, and I thank all of you for your suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why our ITMs are complemented by Jobs Transformation Maps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They help to equip our workers with the relevant skills to take on new jobs as their firms and industries transform.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We work closely with our Institutes of Higher Learning to ensure that fresh graduates from our ITEs, Polytechnics and Universities are equipped with these skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We pay special attention to mid-careerists, especially those in their 40s and 50s, as we recognise that it is harder for them to find jobs if they are displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we work closely with employers and unions on training, reskilling, upskilling and career conversion opportunities for this group.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand the concern amongst those in temporary jobs because they are worried that once COVID-19 is over, they may not have jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our economy recovers, there will be increased demand for workers and more jobs will be created.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are monitoring this carefully to ensure that those in temporary jobs now will be emplaced into permanent positions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har mentioned the good outcomes of this scheme in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In sum, Singapore will never be a large market or the cheapest place to do business.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But what has made Singapore an attractive value proposition for investors is our overall systems competitiveness: rule of law, strong intellectual property protections, connectivity to regional and global markets, an innovative and skilled workforce and, importantly, the strong spirit of tripartite partnership between the Government, unions and employers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to strengthen all of these factors to ensure we build a stronger and more vibrant economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will also build a fairer and more inclusive society because we want to progress, not individually or for our own families, but for our larger Singapore family.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: COVID-19 has deepened existing social inequalities on a global scale.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Across the world, the lower-income and lower-skilled workers suffered the most from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: COVID-19 has also exposed the vulnerabilities of certain segments of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The support that the Government has provided to households and individuals during this period have helped to cushion the impact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But beyond the immediate support, we can and we will do more to address the stresses and strains brought about by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will, therefore, continue to review our social safety nets, paying attention to groups that have been set back during this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who become unemployed, our current support goes beyond ComCare or the COVID-19 Recovery Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It includes a wide range of active labour market policy measures, like job-matching and skills training opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will study how we can provide more help for those who lose their jobs, with continued focus on employment facilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Labour Movement will continue to be an important partner in these efforts, as Mr Abdul Samad and many others have also mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also value the contributions of our caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduced the Home Caregiving Grant recently to defray the costs of caregiving expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to see how we can better support our caregivers, together with the social infrastructure needed for an ageing population.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the rise of the gig economy, we will examine how we can boost protections and strengthen the financial resilience of self-employed persons.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes support for skills upgrading and transition to regular employment for those who wish to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are some of the areas that we are now reviewing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the journey towards building a fairer and more inclusive society goes beyond redistribution and the provision of social assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all have a part to play to ensure social mobility, opportunity and, importantly, dignity for every worker.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must put maximum effort to help every worker earn a fair wage and be accorded due respect for their contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is with this in mind the Government, unions and employers have been collaborating closely to raise the wages and enhance the employability of our lower-wage workers, as well as to improve their working conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Workgroup will release its recommendations in due course and we are confident that these will lead to tangible and beneficial outcomes for our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to regularly review the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme, which works hand in hand with the PWM, to raise the incomes of our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Helping our workers is a continuous endeavour that cannot be accomplished by Government efforts alone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will partner our unions, communities, employers and the workers themselves to ensure that we continue to protect the livelihoods of the most vulnerable amongst us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: COVID-19 has also taken a toll on our mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I assure Dr Tan Yia Swam, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Raeesah Khan who spoke on this issue that the Government takes very seriously the issue of mental health of our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is chaired by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and this task force will bring together the capabilities and capacities of different agencies to coordinate and oversee this important effort.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together with our healthcare professionals and social service agencies, we have stepped up efforts and invested significant resources to enhance the mental well-being of Singaporeans and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The focus areas include awareness, prevention, destigmatisation of mental health issues and treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also take care of the mental well-being of our migrant workers, which is an issue raised by Mr Louis Ng and Mr Mohd Fahmi.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For all of this work, the Government can only do so much alone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will need Singaporeans to step forward and contribute your ideas, talents and energies, so that, together, we can do more to help the disadvantaged and vulnerable in our community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us rally together to build a Singapore where we develop the full potential of every citizen, where every person is respected and valued, and no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will put sustainability at the heart of our recovery, as Ms Mariam Jaafar suggested just now.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Earlier this year, we launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is our national roadmap for a better and greener future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It sets out ambitious sectoral targets to green our living environment, use cleaner energy sources and be more resource-efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As an alternative-energy disadvantaged country, this is a very ambitious aspiration to be net zero, but we are working very hard to make this happen.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also investing in new technologies that can help reduce our waste and emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, all of us must all do our part by adjusting our consumption patterns and making changes to our everyday lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The transition will not be easy and it is not going to be costless.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are also many opportunities to pursue from a green and sustainable Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sustainability will be a new growth area because it cuts across different industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can have green transport, green buildings, green power, a whole range of different new areas to explore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some areas like renewable power, there will, naturally, be constraints on how much we can scale up within Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can be a hub for the financing of projects in the region and even worldwide and we can be a carbon services hub to complement Asia's decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a difficult transition to make, but there are significant opportunities as well, as we enter into the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Building a more vibrant economy, a fairer society and a greener nation – these are all ambitious long-term goals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will take significant resources, billions of dollars.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To make these plans a reality, to achieve that, we need a sustainable fiscal strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The G20 consists of the major economies that make up more than 80% of the world's economy, including many of the world's advanced economies, all with high per capita GDP and standards of living.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But nearly all are grappling with annual deficits and rising public debt, and COVID-19 has worsened their fiscal positions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, increase public spending on healthcare or welfare schemes, all with the best of intentions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But before long, entitlement spending balloons sharply as the economy matures and the population ages, outpacing the ability to raise revenues to cover these spending obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A country turns to borrowing to finance its annual deficits, year after year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this ends up quickly in a downward fiscal spiral.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is more worrying is that societal norms and individual expectations change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It becomes politically very challenging to roll back any benefit and to raise taxes, or even to mention it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a tendency to short-change the future and to overspend on the present.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we must always resist the siren song of easy money and we must do our part to uphold a culture of fiscal responsibility and stewardship.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our constitutional fiscal rules seek to achieve that by imposing strict discipline on how we go about spending and using our reserves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a framework that enables us to safeguard our reserves, while achieving a fair and judicious balance between the interests of today and tomorrow; a balance between spending for today's needs and saving for the future needs of today's generation and generations to come.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It does not mean that the rules can never be changed; I have said that before.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we should do so only after very careful consideration and take measured steps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we debated and amended the Net Investment Returns, or NIR framework, not too long ago in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We made a considered long-term decision that balanced the needs of present and future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The NIR framework would make a very substantial contribution to the Government's annual Budget, but it was not meant to cover every funding need.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Therefore, we should not, at the first sign of need, push for changes in the rules now, just to take the easy way out and avoid having to raise tax revenues to meet our growing recurrent expenditure needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That would not be the responsible thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Prof Hoon Hian Teck both highlighted, we will have to raise revenues in order to meet our rising expenditure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Rising expenditure for very meritorious reasons, for all the things that we talked about: our economy, a fairer inclusive society, a greener nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In deciding the timing of any tax increases, including a GST rate increase, the Government will take into account our fiscal needs as well as the prevailing economic conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Chua suggested that maybe the Government could consider other taxes instead of GST.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The truth of the matter is that we need both.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It reflects the support we aspire to provide for every Singaporean: better healthcare for our elderly and for ourselves as we grow old.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And because these are broad-based needs, we should fund them using a broad-based tax like GST.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As such, we have been increasing other revenue sources over the years, be it income tax, property tax or buyer's stamp duty.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will continue to review these and other tax options for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should just make a point of clarification; it is slightly technical.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Louis Chua mentioned just now that SMEs contributed 29% of corporate income tax but accounted for just 9% of accounting profit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the suggestion is that SMEs pay disproportionately more in tax than non-SMEs; because 29% of corporate income tax, but just 9% of accounting profit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because, firstly, when we look at the accounting profit for all companies, it includes profits and losses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is the bottom line, it is the summation of the bottom line.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Number two, corporate income tax is levied on chargeable income, not accounting profits.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And Mr Louis Chua, I think, should know accountancy and that chargeable income is not the same as accounting profits.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You have to make tax adjustments, like non-tax deductibles, expenses like depreciation or capital allowances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Only the companies with positive chargeable income need to pay corporate income tax.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those with losses can carry forward their losses to offset future years' corporate income tax liability.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, close to 60% of all SMEs do not pay corporate income tax and it is quite clear from the data.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have replied to Parliamentary Questions as well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is quite clear from the data that SMEs have a lower tax burden than non-SMEs or the larger companies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The effective tax rate for SMEs is 3% but the effective tax rate for non-SMEs is 8% to 10%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our system is such that SMEs have a lower tax burden.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Going back to GST, some have expressed concerns that the GST is regressive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, again, we cannot look at GST in isolation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our GST system is unique in that it is tied to a permanent GST Voucher scheme, where we offset the GST for lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we also absorb GST for publicly subsidised healthcare and education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, we will enhance the permanent GST Voucher scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, not just the temporary but the permanent layer to strengthen support for lower- to middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, concerns about regressivity have been mitigated and will continue to be, as we plan for the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, remember that our public services and subsidies are designed to provide more help for the lower- and middle-income.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Put together, the outcome is that the higher-income groups pay more taxes than the benefits they receive, while the lower- and middle-income groups receive significantly more benefits than the taxes they pay.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we ensure our taxes and transfers remain fair and progressive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it will be anchored in a system of sound and sustainable finances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will be remembered as the time when our usually bustling CBD laid empty; when we had to work from home; when we had to meet with our friends and loved ones over a screen.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it will also be remembered as the time we saw the best of Singaporeans amidst adversity and tough conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have much going for us today and much more we can look forward to in the journey ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us harness our collective strengths, keep striving to do better and write many more chapters of our Singapore Story together.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Actually, the last question in my speech has not been answered, regarding whether the Government will be providing a reimbursement to the Town Councils for the extra manpower expenses for the SafeEntry access management.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think that is what we will do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not just about this particular measure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a new requirement, but there have been many other things.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: And I was just wondering if the Minister will be able to share with us the breakdown in terms of the chargeable income, as broken down between SMEs and non-SMEs.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think that will also give us a better understanding.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: As the Minister has shared, there is a difference between statutory income, assessible income as well as chargeable income.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Having this additional information, which I also note that the Minister shared in my other Parliamentary Question (PQ) yesterday, I think that will help us to understand the numbers better.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think the other clarification is, I was just wondering if it is incorrect to say that SMEs bear a higher proportion of the tax burden, given that just based on the numbers I am looking at, I am looking at $4.8 billion of corporate income tax paid by SMEs as a proportion of the $16 billion of corporate income tax paid by all companies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, that is roughly about 29% versus SMEs being about 99% in terms of enterprise count.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Well, I think to Mr Louis Chua's question, we will be happy to provide the figures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There will be detailed data and we can provide all this in reply to a written question.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chua has filed some of them and we have been forthcoming with the data.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will be quite happy to put it out, distinguishing between, as I have said, accounting profits and chargeable income.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A quick question on an issue which some Members brought up, which is foreign workers who are currently still in the dormitories.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand they get to go to certain facilities within a closed-off area in the dormitory for rest and recreation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is there also a roadmap for them when they can also be re-integrated into the larger community?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: They have been, as we know, locked down for a long time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is also a question raised by Mr Louis Ng and Mr Mohd Fahmi.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I did not elaborate on this in my speech, but just to say that we are very, very mindful of the mental well-being of these workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We know that they have been subject to these restrictions for quite a long time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For now, the concern is that because of the large clusters that we are seeing in our community, we are quite worried about how they might catch the virus if they were to go out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Having said that, the vaccination rates amongst migrant workers in the dorms are now very high and it is getting higher.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is something that the MTF is looking at.
